From your MR and coloc results to a benchmark verdict

Source: vignettes/articles/tutorial.Rmd
tutorial.Rmd

This page walks through one run of karim_pos() with four made-up candidates, one for each thing that can happen to a row: it meets the criteria, it misses a threshold, it lacks a value, or its coloc result cannot be told apart from another. Then it shows how to fix the last two, and how the bundled reference fills in values for a real gene. All output below comes from running the code.

1. What you give, what you get

karim_pos() takes two tables:

  • mr: one row per cis-pQTL MR result, with mr_id, the gene (target_id), the indication (indication_id, a MeSH ID), the pQTL assay (exposure_id), the outcome GWAS (outcome_id), the genome build, a locus_id and the p-value mr_p.
  • coloc: one row per colocalization result, with coloc_id, the same four keys (exposure_id, outcome_id, build, locus_id) and the posterior probability h4.

Rows are joined on the four keys. Nothing is joined by position, and nothing is guessed. For each MR row you get a status, the matched coloc row, and, if the row meets the criteria of Karim et al., the historical launch proportion of their support group.

2. Four candidates 

library(geneticPoS)

loc <- function(id) data.frame(exposure_id = paste0("P", id), outcome_id = "D1",
                               build = "GRCh38", locus_id = paste0("L", id))
mr <- rbind(
  cbind(loc(1), mr_id = "M1", target_id = "G1", indication_id = "UC", mr_p = 4e-10,
        l2g_share = 0.67, mesh_similarity = 0.91, measured = TRUE),   # meets every threshold
  cbind(loc(2), mr_id = "M2", target_id = "G2", indication_id = "UC", mr_p = 1e-5,
        l2g_share = 0.80, mesh_similarity = 0.95, measured = TRUE),   # MR p-value too weak
  cbind(loc(3), mr_id = "M3", target_id = "G3", indication_id = "UC", mr_p = 2e-11,
        l2g_share = NA,   mesh_similarity = 0.90, measured = TRUE),   # no L2G share
  cbind(loc(4), mr_id = "M4", target_id = "G4", indication_id = "UC", mr_p = 3e-12,
        l2g_share = 0.60, mesh_similarity = 0.85, measured = TRUE))   # two coloc rows fit
coloc <- rbind(
  cbind(loc(1), coloc_id = "K1",  h4 = 0.93),
  cbind(loc(2), coloc_id = "K2",  h4 = 0.95),
  cbind(loc(3), coloc_id = "K3",  h4 = 0.90),
  cbind(loc(4), coloc_id = "K4a", h4 = 0.90),
  cbind(loc(4), coloc_id = "K4b", h4 = 0.70))

res <- karim_pos(mr, coloc)
res$candidates[, c("mr_id", "mr_p", "l2g_share", "h4", "status", "missing_fields",
                   "match_basis", "reference_group", "historical_launch_rate")]
  mr_id  mr_p l2g_share   h4             status missing_fields       match_basis reference_group historical_launch_rate
1    M1 4e-10      0.67 0.93     thresholds_met                exact_identifiers       supported              0.5555556
2    M2 1e-05      0.80 0.95 thresholds_not_met                exact_identifiers            <NA>                     NA
3    M3 2e-11        NA 0.90     missing_inputs      l2g_share exact_identifiers            <NA>                     NA
4    M4 3e-12      0.60   NA    coloc_ambiguous                             <NA>            <NA>                     NA

3. Reading the status

status What it means What to do
thresholds_met Matched, and MR p ≤ 0.05/47,000,000, H4 ≥ 0.8, L2G share ≥ 0.5, MeSH similarity ≥ 0.8, measured target. Gets reference_group = "supported" and the launch proportion. Read the proportion as a past group outcome (section 6).
thresholds_not_met Matched and complete, but at least one threshold is missed (here M2: MR p = 1e-5). No reference group is assigned. Nothing to fix. One analysis failing a threshold does not by itself put the gene–indication pair in the comparison group.
missing_inputs A value is missing; missing_fields names it (here l2g_share). Supply it (section 4).
coloc_ambiguous / coloc_unmatched More than one, or no, coloc row has the same keys. Add signal_id to both tables, or link the rows yourself (section 4).
link_conflict Rows you linked disagree on a key. Check the identifiers.
outside_pqtl_reference qtl_type says the result is not a pQTL, for example an eQTL. The benchmark does not cover it.
outside_measured_background measured is FALSE: the target is not measured by the pQTL assay. The benchmark does not cover it.
invalid_input A p-value, H4, L2G share or similarity is outside [0, 1]. Fix the value.

4. Fix what can be fixed

A missing value (M3). Pass it in metadata, keyed by the row of the MR table (source_row, counted from one). metadata only fills missing values; a value that conflicts with the table is refused.

res2 <- karim_pos(mr, coloc,
                  metadata = list(mr = data.frame(source_row = 3, l2g_share = 0.7)))
res2$candidates[, c("mr_id", "l2g_share", "l2g_share_source", "status")]
  mr_id l2g_share l2g_share_source             status
1    M1      0.67             user     thresholds_met
2    M2      0.80             user thresholds_not_met
3    M3      0.70             user     thresholds_met
4    M4      0.60             user    coloc_ambiguous

l2g_share_source records where each value came from (user here).

Two coloc rows fit (M4). If your tables have several signals per locus, give both a signal_id. If you have checked in the source papers which coloc row belongs to the MR row, link them and state the evidence:

links <- data.frame(mr_id = "M4", coloc_id = "K4a",
                    basis = "Same signal in the source paper, Table 2")
res3 <- karim_pos(mr, coloc, links = links)
res3$candidates[, c("mr_id", "matched_coloc_id", "h4", "status", "match_basis", "reference_group")]
  mr_id matched_coloc_id   h4             status       match_basis reference_group
1    M1               K1 0.93     thresholds_met exact_identifiers       supported
2    M2               K2 0.95 thresholds_not_met exact_identifiers            <NA>
3    M3               K3 0.90     missing_inputs exact_identifiers            <NA>
4    M4              K4a 0.90     thresholds_met    user_confirmed       supported

match_basis now says user_confirmed: the link is yours, not the package’s.

5. Let the bundled reference fill in values

The package carries a processed snapshot of the Karim reference. For a real gene symbol, indication MeSH ID and outcome GWAS ID it looks up the MeSH similarity and whether the target is measured, and it says so in the *_source columns. Here, IL23R and Crohn’s disease (MeSH D003424, GWAS GCST004132), with no values supplied:

keys <- data.frame(exposure_id = "IL23R.pQTL", outcome_id = "GCST004132",
                   build = "GRCh37", locus_id = "rs11581607")
mr    <- cbind(keys, mr_id = "IL23R_CD", target_id = "IL23R", indication_id = "D003424", mr_p = 5.9e-93)
coloc <- cbind(keys, coloc_id = "c1", h4 = 0.993)

r <- karim_pos(mr, coloc)
r$candidates[, c("l2g_share", "l2g_share_source", "mesh_similarity", "mesh_similarity_source",
                 "measured", "measured_source", "status", "missing_fields")]
  l2g_share l2g_share_source mesh_similarity mesh_similarity_source measured measured_source         status missing_fields
1        NA      unavailable               1          karim_mapping     TRUE  karim_measured missing_inputs      l2g_share

The L2G share is specific to your locus, so the snapshot does not guess it. Give it, with its source, and the row reaches the support group:

r2 <- karim_pos(mr, coloc, metadata = list(mr = list(l2g_share = 0.55)))
r2$candidates[, c("l2g_share", "l2g_share_source", "status", "reference_group", "historical_launch_rate")]
  l2g_share l2g_share_source         status reference_group historical_launch_rate
1      0.55             user thresholds_met       supported              0.5555556

The independent check extracts the coefficients for this pair from public data and explains where 0.55 comes from.

6. What the number means 

res3$benchmark[, c("group", "phase1_n", "launched_n", "relative_success", "rs_lower", "rs_upper")]
       group phase1_n launched_n relative_success rs_lower rs_upper
1  supported       36         20             5.24     3.88     7.07
2 comparison     7164        760             5.24     3.88     7.07

Of 36 gene–indication pairs in the support group of Karim v2 Figure 1a, 20 went from phase 1 to launch (55.56%); of 7,164 pairs in the comparison group, 760 did (10.6%). The relative success is 5.24 (3.88 to 7.07). These are past group outcomes. thresholds_met puts a candidate in the group that the numbers describe; it does not make 55.56% the probability that this candidate launches, and the package does not evaluate how well it predicts a single candidate.
